text.p: Northeast Utilities said Tuesday it completed all necessary work to allow the Independent Corrective Action Verification Process (ICAVP) to begin for its Millstone 3 nuclear power unit.
The ICAVP is seen as an important step in winning permission from federal regulators to restart its three Millstone plants, which have been closed for safety reasons since March 1996.
Northeast has said it intends to have Millstone 3 ready for restart by the end of September, pending approval by federal regulators.

ICAVP is the Nuclear Regulatory Commission's independent method of checking the quality and thoroughness of Northeast's work to assure the design and configuration of the plant is correct, and that its corrective action process is effective.

"This is an extensive process and it means a great deal to us that we successfully met our first major restart milestone," Northeast Nuclear Energy Co. Chief Executive Bruce Kenyon said in a statement.

ICAVP readiness requires the power plant to finalize its internal audit plan and receive NRC approval; identify issues and necessary modifications for at least 50 percent of safety and risk significant systems and associated engineering programs; and receive NRC approval for the ICAVP contractor, among other procedures.
Northeast has said it intends to have all three of its Millstone plants ready for restart by early 1998, pending NRC approval.
